result.summary: Independently re-verified TEST-DESIGNER's 78d4101 pass on capability_gate_test.exs. All 7 of docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-167 acceptance criteria have runnable, passing test coverage traceable through test/specs/REQ-167.md's T1-T6 to named tests in capability_gate_test.exs (AC1/WASM-06 -> describe 'AC1: a module granted only var:read cannot import platform_call_service'; AC2/whitelist-by-inspection -> describe 'AC2: build_import_table/1 builds a genuine whitelist from the manifest'; AC3/filesystem-surface -> describe 'AC3: the req163-named filesystem surface is rejected under any manifest' using priv/wasm_fixtures/req167_path_open.wat's wasi_snapshot_preview1/path_open surface, never the literal wasi:filesystem/types string; AC4/AC5/AC6 moduledoc content -> describe 'moduledoc content restates WASM-07 per design section 7', three tests reading Code.fetch_docs/1 directly; 'mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass' -> re-run myself, see below). No @tag :skip or @tag :pending anywhere in the file; no 'TODO: implement test' text. Fixtures (req167_no_imports.wat, req167_path_open.wat, req167_platform_call_only.wat, req167_unregistered_import.wat) are each a small self-contained inline WAT module with no shared mutable state, no dependency on another test's side effects, and no ordering requirement between tests (async: false is a NIF-concurrency-safety choice documented in the file's own moduledoc, not a hidden ordering dependency) -- each test independently reads its own fixture file and calls a pure function or a fresh start_instance/2. No hardcoded secrets or connection strings in any test/fixture file. Ran `mix test test/letflow/engine/wasm/capability_gate_test.exs` myself against the unmodified commit: 'Result: 18 passed' (0 failures), quoted below. Independently re-applied 3 of TEST-DESIGNER's 6 reported mutations directly against lib/letflow/engine/wasm/capability_gate.ex in the working tree (not trusting the report's own numbers), each followed by a full mix test run and a git checkout revert, verified clean after each: (1) AC6 empty-manifest-shape mutation (Enum.reduce/3 accumulator seeded with %{"env" => %{}} instead of %{}) -- measured 17/18 passed, 1 failed, and the failure is exactly 'an empty capability list produces exactly %{}, not a namespace-present-but-empty map' asserting left: %{"env" => %{}}, right: %{} -- matches the report's claim exactly. (2) AC4 pid-liveness mutation (GenServer.stop(pid) inserted into the {:ok, {:ok, pid}} success branch before returning) -- measured 14/18 passed, 4 failed; the new test 'the returned pid is alive and usable immediately after a successful call' fails cleanly on `assert Process.alive?(pid)` (Expected truthy, got false), a direct, unambiguous assertion rather than the incidental double-stop crash the report describes the OLD suite catching it via -- confirms the new test genuinely strengthens detection precision as claimed, not merely duplicating existing incidental coverage. (3) AC2/WASI-regression mutation (added wasi: true to the Wasmex.start_link/1 call) -- the single most security-relevant finding in this run, re-applied and measured directly: 16/18 passed, 2 failed, both failures are the AC3/path_open tests, each returning {:ok, pid} instead of the expected {:error, {:instantiation_denied, {:unresolved_import, "wasi_snapshot_preview1", "path_open"}}} -- i.e. a hardcoded wasi: true genuinely lets path_open resolve via wasmex's native WASI implementation, and the EXISTING (not new) AC3 tests already catch this because they assert the specific unresolved_import tuple rather than a bare {:error, _}. This is a real, security-critical regression-detection property already present in the suite, not an overclaimed finding. All three mutations were reverted via `git checkout -- lib/letflow/engine/wasm/capability_gate.ex` immediately after measurement; `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` and `git diff --stat lib/letflow/engine/wasm/capability_gate.ex` were both empty after every single revert, and a final `mix test` re-run confirmed 18/18 green on the untouched implementation before writing this verdict. No coverage gap found; no overclaimed finding found. mix letflow.lint_handoffs run against the full handoff tree: 0 new violations (25 pre-existing grandfathered violations traced to ISS-0190, none introduced by this handoff).
